utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the Prosecution would like to raise a preliminary matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. The first matter relates to yesterday's decision by the Appeals Chamber with respect to adjudicated facts. While we are still reviewing the decision, it is clear that approximately 40 facts have been now vacated by the Appeals Chamber. The Prosecution is proposing that it be given approximately a week and that next Tuesday, I would report to the Chamber what, if any, implications there are for this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's fine with the Chamber, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The second matter I want to bring your attention to and I'm not seeking or making any applications at this time. The Chamber will undoubtedly have heard about the new mass grave that has been discovered and that is in Tomasica mine. We had a report from people working on this project yesterday. As of yesterday, over 470 bodies have been recovered. Remarkably, a number of these bodies still have soft tissue and adipose so the pathology reports should be available to reveal important evidence about how these people died. This is of particular relevance to this case for two reasons. One, there have been approximately ten preliminary identifications of victims. That is, identifications based upon identity documents found with the corpses. Ten of those are victim -- named victims in this case. It's also relevant because if the Chamber were to look at an entry in the Mladic diary of the 27th of May, 1993 - and that's P358 in evidence at e-court P154 - the Chamber will see that Mr. Mladic has a conversation with police officials about -- regarding 5.000 bodies that are at the Tomasica mine, so there was the direct link to this case. We are in very regular contact with local officials and ICMP. There are about to begin the process of conducting DNA identifications which they -- my last report with respect to when they had 374 bodies, they believed they would have that process completed in the beginning of January. I imagine with the extra 100 bodies it will be a bit longer. John Clark, who testified before this Chamber is -- has already made plans to go and do some of the pathology work. So I'm just bringing this to the Chamber's attention. We are considering our obligations and our position with respect to this very important evidence that's been uncovered today and will be -- continue to be uncovered over the coming days and we may have applications in the future. But, again, I just wanted to bring the Chamber up to speed, as it were, on this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. Earlier reference was made to P358 in evidence at e-court P154. One of them most likely is the page number --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and the other one is the exhibit number. What is the page number?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It is page 154 in e-court in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I have one application. If I could go into private session for that application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. While the witness is brought in, I briefly deal with the same matter as you started with today, Mr. Groome. On the 12th of November, the Appeals Chamber decided on the Defence's appeal with regard to adjudicated facts, and as a result of the Appeals Chamber's decision, the Chamber hereby decides that the adjudicated facts listed in numbers 1 through 3 of the disposition of the Appeals Chamber's decision are no longer judicially noticed. The Chamber instructs the Prosecution to inform the Chamber and the Defence in the time you told us, Mr. Groome, about what action, if any, it intends to take as a result of this decision. But the instruction was anticipated already by yourself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps needless to say, but I nevertheless remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Examination by Ms. Marcus [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And good morning, Dr. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, Dr. Tabeau has prepared some slides to facilitate the presentation of her evidence. The slides have been assigned P2792, MFI. I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart to assist us in displaying these slides in Sanction during the -- during the examination. Ms. Stewart, could I please have slide 1. While that is coming up, Your Honour, I'd note for the record that there are two acronyms which will be commonly used in this examination. One is POD, which already was introduced yesterday. That is proof of death. And the other is DU, which stands for the Demographics Unit. That is the team that Dr. Tabeau has been leading. Could I please have slide 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, can you explain to us, please, briefly the import of slide 2.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this slide, reference is made to the first demographic expert report presented at this Tribunal. It was a report on Srebrenica victims, victims of the fall of Srebrenica. It was presented in the Krstic case in the year 2000. In the table some numbers from this report are presented, predominantly it is the Srebrenica missing number, 7.475, which was the essential result of this report. This number was made exclusively based on records of missing persons. At that time, only 68 individuals were identified. It wasn't a DNA identification. It was a classical identification method and the overall per cent of identified was less than 1 per cent. So, even though this report was seen at that time as a very significant result of the office, that the list like that could be made, there was a feeling that there is a need to take next steps to improve the evidence about the victims of the fall of Srebrenica. And our thinking at the time was that improvements must be seen in cross-referencing the evidence on the missing with the evidence on the exhumed persons and identified persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I please have slide 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before we move to the next one, I have one question. There is an entry PIP with a number. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The PIP stands for Podrinje Identification Project. It is a project run by local authorities was established with the involvement of the ICMP in Bosnia-Herzegovina. It is a project that is focussed on the identification of the victims on the first place of the fall of Srebrenica. This refers to the source for 68 identifications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can I ask one or two additional questions. The number of 9 means that persons initially reported as being missing have found to have been survivors. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Initially reported as missing related to the fall of Srebrenica, were confirmed as survivors in other sources and excluded from the statistics in this report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have the accepted victims which is 7.477 which is number higher than the missing number of missing persons.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The two, missing persons and identified, overlap largely but not one to one. So obviously there were two additional victims from the identifications that were accepted in addition to the missing persons from the OTP list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we have the per cent identified. Is that the 68 against the 7.475 or 7.477?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it is related in the - if I'm not wrong - in the missing persons exclusively. These percentages can be calculated in various ways, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which has lost --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But which has lost much of its importance because now we have a higher number of accepted victims not necessarily identified.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think we will be talking about these numbers later today so this number will be updated. This was our springboard for all the next reports, next analysis completed over the years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On slide 3, Dr. Tabeau, could you please explain what this demonstrates?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- in this slide visualise three universes: The universe of missing persons which is red, the universe of exhumed human remains which is blue, and the universe of identified persons in the colour green. Certain questions are addressed here that can be answered in research that is exploring each of these universes separately, but the essential question -- essential question is: What is the result of the comparison of a merge, of an integration, of the three universes, the missing, exhumed and identified? This question is not yet answered in this slide. This slide shows the sources and the research questions that can be answered on each of the group of sources.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this slide represent a POD analysis of sources applicable both to Srebrenica as well as to the POD analysis for the rest of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is the same foundation, conceptual foundation, analytical foundation, that has been used in both projects, in the Srebrenica projects and POD project completed for this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I please ask Ms. Stewart to show slide 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, please tell us what we are looking at here.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This slide takes us one step further and shows the overlap of the three groups of sources. Essentially we are talking about cross-referencing the missing persons records with records of exhumed persons and records of identified persons. Ideally we would like to see the red part, the heart of the cross-referencing, very big. Ideally we would like to see one-to-one correspondence between each of these sources. In this way we could tell what happened to every missing person from the moment the person was reported missing to the moment the remains of this person were exhumed from a mass or other grave, and identified, either classically or through the DNA analysis, to close the circle of questions related to the fate of the person. In practice, there is no one-to-one correspondence. The red part grows over time, when more and more data becomes available and more analysis becomes available, but because of this situation of war situation, it is not possible to obtain one-to-one correspondence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I ask Ms. Stewart for slide 5 please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, it not possible or is it not always possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have never obtained one-to-one correspondence in my practice. In my work on victims theoretically it is possible, but because sources are so incomplete, sources are compiled according to the different standards. There are also technical problems because of that, so this linkage of sources practically remains below the 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Slide 5, please, Ms. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain the POD sources which are shown on this slide, please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this slide, reference is made to the POD project completed for the Mladic case. I use the same colours on this slide as in the circles in the previous slides. As sources for missing persons, ICRC records of the missing were used as well as BCMP records were used. BCMP stands for the Bosnian Commission for Missing Persons. The blue circle, exhumations, is represented by very large documentation from exhumations related to the incidents reported in the schedules to the Mladic indictment; that would be exhumation reports, on-site investigative reports, autopsy reports, and related death certificates. And the third group, identification of victims, was analysed based on identification reports mainly classical, some were available as DNA-based identifications. In addition to these major core sources we also additionally used sources related to the witness statements, that would be court rulings from local courts in Bosnia and Herzegovina and those that related based on witness statements. And very importantly, we also had completed a search in a very large database established in my unit, the so-called integrated database. Integrated database is a merge of a number of very large sources reporting on war victims, sources of which we will be talking later perhaps today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To clarify a bit, when you say at the top of this slide "verification of scheduled victims," that refers to the scheduled victims lists that the OTP had put together; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Demographics Unit, the DU, use --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers are kindly asked to pause between question and answer. This is really complex and we need a little more time to interpret everything correctly. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: My apologies, I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the DU use witness evidence from the Mladic case in its POD analysis for the Mladic case?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now this is a slide of sources, POD sources. How would you compare, again briefly, based on this slide, the sources used for the POD analysis for Srebrenica with the POD sources used for the rest of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rest of Bosnia. You mean the POD project for the Mladic case, right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, basically, as I said, it is the same type of sources and the same -- same type of methodological approach that was applied in both cases. For Srebrenica, the focus was on missing persons and DNA-based identification records. Through the DNA identifications, information became available on the exhumations and grave-sites from a large group of sources that were not discussed in our Srebrenica report but were taken by others. In this particular case, in this particular case it is that in addition to the missing persons records and identification records, we work directly with sources from exhumations. So this package is more complete in that sense because it shows all three aspects of the tracking process in one report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it from your answer that there have been fewer DNA identifications related to the municipalities than there were from Srebrenica. If that is -- if -- if my understanding is correct, can you explain briefly why, if you know.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. There were fewer DNA identifications available for the POD victims. POD victims are all coming from a different war episode than Srebrenica, and we are talking about earlier -- early months of the war 1992 versus Srebrenica 1995. Srebrenica has been the highest priority of the ICMP for a long time, so this was at the heart of the identification process of this organisation. And obviously, we could see the results of this kind of prioritising in the sense that very many DNA identifications have become available for Srebrenica victim and many less for victims from other episodes of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you a hypothetical question just for our understanding. Let's say victim A has one source that provides evidence of the circumstances of his death as compared with victim B who has five sources that provide evidence of the circumstances of his death. How would you compare your confidence in the results of the determination of the fate of victim A with that for victim B?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one remark, you, of course, didn't say anything about what kind of documents are available, the five documents versus the one available. It's relevant what kind of sources we have at our disposal, but I think the main point, assuming that these documents, the one and the five, all confirm consistently the fact that a person died in a certain situation, in certain circumstances. Generally the question is what is the importance of using multiple sources versus a single source in this type of work, and the answer is that in the war situations, it's very hard to be sure of what happened and how it happened. Because the documentation of this is very fragmented, has gaps, has miscommunications. It's the common practice. So when we talk about the fate of victims and we are trying to prove what happened, it's important, it's essential, to use as many relevant and reliable sources as possible that they would compare, corroborate the findings related to this victim. So this increases our confidence in the result obtained.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Ms. Stewart, can I please have slide 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, can you tell us a bit about the obstacles to the POD analysis conducted by the DU.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This slide lists a number of such obstacles. We are talking about comparing sources, about linking sources, which means we are talking about declaring records of information representing the same person in different sources as consistent. It would be a very easy job if we had a numerical characteristic for every case the same in every source compared and the linkage would be very easy, just comparing a number we would quickly and with a -- with a set of links establish that. But it is not the case we are talking about in -- in the POD project and also not in the Srebrenica projects. The comparison is done based on descriptive items, like names, like dates of birth, place of birth, and there are issues relates to comparing descriptive items, like spelling mistakes, like swapping names, father's with first name, like misreporting dates in related sources of information. We are talking about occasional duplications and we are talking about the possibility of survivors listed among the victims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you do to overcome these obstacles to enable you to reach conclusions with confidence?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have done a lot of effort and spent a lot of time on removing inconsistencies, differences, different formats between the sources, checking for duplicates, checking for survivors, all this is described in our reports. I would refer the Chamber and everybody to the annexes of the 2009 integrated Srebrenica report as well as to the annexes from the Slobodan Milosevic report. But the essential message, yes, that next to the other work, there is a need to use a reference standard, a good reference standard, a source that could serve as such that would be telling how to see inconsistencies in the reporting. And such a reference standard has become the 1991 population census, the last pre-war population census available for Bosnia and Herzegovina, which was the core of our information system in the Demographic Unit with this source, the census, all sources on victims, other sources, were always compared and links were established between the sources using this reference census.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I ask you, Ms. Tabeau, to explain the acronyms used in the second bullet point, especially those in red.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am in the second bullet point referring to the record IDs, numeric or alphanumeric record IDs from the three sources. In ICRC data, the so-called BAZ number is used, which is not exclusively a numeric number. It's alphanumeric but a numeric part is available. Protocol ID, case ID, ICMP ID are three identifiers of cases used in the ICMP data on DNA identification of victims. And case ID, which is actually the label attached to the -- to a set of remains exhumed from a given site, is also used in exhumation records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What does BAZ stand for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is just -- it doesn't have a meaning as such. It is -- I cannot -- what is the full name, it is just a symbol which probably has a meaning, but it is relevant from the point of view of how it is used. It is just a reference number for every case. Every case has a number which begins with the BAZ, or BAS if misspelled, or slightly different form, plus a number and the -- the whole string of characters, BAZ plus a number, is a record ID in the ICRC data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I please have slide 7.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, you started to talk a bit in your last -- in your answer a few answers ago about the major reference sources. Can you -- here on this slide you set them out. Can you explain how are these major reference sources related to the other POD sources you discussed when we were looking at slide 5.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Population census, 1991, for the entire country, 4.4 million records was used as the central list of individuals as a reference source to compare the names and other personal details with. Second bullet point, OSCE voters' registers, 1997, 1998, 2000, 2.5 million each were used a source on post-war survivors and were searched through in order to verify whether or not victims have survived. BH government register of internally displaced person and refugees, 580.000 records served the same purpose. In addition, we in our work systematically used military lists of all three armies - ABiH, HVO and VRS - in order to flag victims to let everybody know who was found on this list versus not. These are basic reference sources for our work.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Ms. Stewart, may I please have slide 8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, you are here today to present three major reports: The POD update report for Srebrenica; the POD report for the municipalities; and the IDPs and refugees report. What is the relationship between the methodological framework for these three reports?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This slide summarises the review routine used by my unit over the years for each of these three types of analysis. It -- any victim lists, missing persons, scheduled victims, other victims lists can be subjected to the same routine as illustrated in this chart. At the core is the population census and the sources on post-war survivors, in case of victims, which are always used with every victim list to begin with to -- to -- to remove inconsistencies and survivors and to prepare for next steps. So in case of IDPs and refugees report, it is the -- the middle part is not so relevant. It is the population census and the cross-referencing of the census with the post-war lists on survivors, predominantly voters' registers, from which we can draw conclusions about population movements during the time of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was just waiting for the translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Ms. Stewart, could you please show slide 9. Your Honours, with that overview that Dr. Tabeau has just presented, I will now focus the next part of my examination on the Srebrenica POD-related expert reports. For the record, Your Honours, the Srebrenica evidence connected with Dr. Tabeau's testimony is as follows. P1900 and P1901, both admitted through Helge Brunborg. P2794, MFI, which is the 2013 Srebrenica update report provided by Dr. Tabeau for the Mladic case. And P2795, MFI, which are the annexes to that update report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, your Srebrenica expert report for this case updates your prior report which was admitted through Helge Brunborg as P1900. Could you please tell us what your 2013 update, which is P2794, MFI, adds to the 2009 report.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2013 Srebrenica report I made focuses exclusively on the analysis of new identifications issued by the ICMP between the time the 2009 integrated report was finished until February 2013. This was the date I used for my report for the Mladic case. So, in total, there was 1.190 new identifications in this period. Of this number, quite a considerable portion have been additionally matched with the 2009 OTP victims list. I suggest we move to the table in order to see the progress. The table is taken from the report, 2009 report, it is Table 12 on page 28. It is not a complete table. It only presents the essential columns from that table. The essential columns being Srebrenica missing, Srebrenica identified, excluded survivors, potential survivors, accepted integrated victims, and per cent identified. We saw the first line of this table earlier today. Now I will be talking about the last line that summarises the progress until this day. So we see the number of Srebrenica missing slightly higher compared to the first initial report from the year 2000. Not very much though. It is a small increase that was added to the initial list. In the second column, in the -- under identified persons, we moved from the 68 identified based on the classical method, to, in total, 6.745 identified persons, including the results from the 2013 report I just made this year. The overlap of this number, 6.745, with the OTP list is 6.603, which you can see from the notes, Note 2, under this table. It's a considerable overlap, and if these two numbers are compared, 6.603 with the number of missing on the -- on the OTP list, 7.692, the resulting per cent is almost 86 per cent. 85.8. So we moved from less than 1 per cent in the first row of the table to 85.8 per cent. The number of excluded potential survivors remained low. It is still 12 today as it used to be since 2005. The integrated number of victims increased from 7.477 to 8.047 victims. These are the latest statistics incorporating the results from my 2013 Srebrenica update.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, in essence, the bottom row on the table we see on the slide is the data emerging from the update for the Mladic case which is an update from the 2009 report admitted through Helge Brunborg as P1900; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I note for the record that Table 12 of the 2009 report, which, as it says here and as Dr. Tabeau says, is on page 28 in English and page 32 in B/C/S of that report, P1900, has also been admitted under number another exhibit number which is P1902. So what we see on the slide in front of us is an update to that exhibit as well. Could I ask Ms. Stewart to show slide 13 please. We're going to skip a few slides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, could I ask you to briefly explain the import of figure 7 that we see in front of us from P1900.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: We don't see the reference on the slide if -- if we can move it a little bit. This figure comes from -- from the 2009 integrated Srebrenica report. It is not new. It is the same figure. This figure would remain almost unchanged when the results would be redone, including the identifications studied recently in the 2013 Srebrenica report, my report for the Mladic case. If we now move the slide to see the title, please. This slide shows certain percentages for three age groups, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59. We can focus exclusively on one age group for the simplicity of explanation. The first one, the brown bars. The brown bars represent Muslim men victims of the fall of Srebrenica as per cent of the 1991 population in their municipalities of residence in 1991. Once again, Muslim men victims as percentage of their 1991 population in their place of residence in 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you're referring to the same age group in the 1991 census.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. It is the same group of men, it is the same exactly group of men. The results are presented based on a linked records. Linked records. So it is the exactly same group of people we are talking about here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the age groups are defined by 1991 or by the 1995 events where they went missing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think most likely 1991 age, but I will double-check because I am not certain. But generally, it doesn't matter that much but it would make a difference in age. I can check this for a tomorrow. I can tell exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It may be important for us to know the age of the men when they went missing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, yeah. With the time they went missing, what age were they, yes. That's the point. So we see on this chart only five municipalities, Srebrenica, Bratunac, Vlasenica, Zvornik, Han Pijesak. These are the five municipalities that were affected most in the fall of Srebrenica. And Srebrenica was by all means the one affected more than any one else. So for Srebrenica for this age group, brown bars, 45-49, we see that about 50 per cent of men originally residing in this municipality in 1991 went missing in the fall of Srebrenica, which is a very significant number and illustrates the scale of suffering of the -- of the Muslim men from this territory. Another finding that can be read from this chart is that Zvornik is affected relatively little compared to Srebrenica. Generally the municipalities located geographically close to Srebrenica were affected more. Zvornik is more distant and the distance from -- geographical distance we think explains why the number for Zvornik is lower.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you what you did take as your criterion for qualifying as a victim? Is that missing, is that identified? Could you tell us what qualifies for being a victim in this table.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think in this table a victim is a missing person on the first place. For the new victims that entered the Srebrenica list, we don't have actually information about the disappearance as specific as for the missing persons because ICMP does not provide this information, so it is predominantly missing persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Dr. Tabeau has provided in her reports extensive additional information on this topic and therefore I will now turn to the proof of death report for the municipalities. Dr. Tabeau's POD expert evidence for municipalities includes the following. The portion of the POD report admitted in the Stanisic and Simatovic case now P2787, MFI; the POD report for the Mladic case, P2796, MFI; the POD annex, P2797, MFI; the clarifications to this annex, P2793, MFI; the addendum to the POD annex pertaining to four victims, P2790, MFI; and, finally, the table of name correspondence, P2791, MFI. Could Ms. Stewart please now show slide 14.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, based upon your knowledge and expertise, what is the significance of conducting an analysis of POD of named victims in cases such as this?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may ask for assistance, I would like to have also transcript on the screen. Is it possible sometimes or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any way that Ms. Tabeau could have on one screen the transcript and on the other the exhibit shown?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it's coming from the Sanction system, we are helpless.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. It's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But a division of work between Ms. Stewart and Ms. Hellman may resolve the problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. It is okay. I can do it without for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And don't hesitate to ask the question to be repeated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I please do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I will do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based upon your knowledge and expertise, what is the significance of conducting an analysis of the POD of named victims in cases such as this case?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the significance is, of course, fundamental because when we know the names of the victims and we are in the position to find them, identify them, in a number of related sources, we can provide lots of useful information that would explain their fate, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The POD report, P2796, MFI, and its annex, P2797, MFI, were the result of an analysis of both POD documents as well as demographic sources which you refer to as the integrated database. Would you say that is accurate?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as we look at slide 14, the top of the page, we see the POD documents at the top, and when we move down, we will see the integrated database at the bottom. With respect to the POD documents at the top of this slide, you list the major types of documents which were analysed. How would you assess your degree of familiarity with the kinds of POD documents which were analysed for the POD report?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think my familiarity in my own eyes is very good. I have been working with these type of documents for a long time. The first POD report I made at this Tribunal dates 2002, so it was a report actually related to the same episode of war to 1992 victims from Autonomous Region of Krajina. Already at the time, the same type of sources were used jointly with missing persons records to draw conclusions about the number of victims and their fate. It's perhaps important to note at this point that there is usually a very large number of the exhumation documents, autopsies, forensic reports, anthropological reports, exhumation reports itself, investigative reports, it is a massive -- massive collection of documents. So it is really very essential when working with these sources to be very clear about how they link to victims scheduled on the lists, to sort out the connections, to accept the relevant documents, to reject irrelevant documents. So the work that we have done on the POD project was meant to bring up this clarity, a picture that will -- that would explain what happened to these people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the course of reviewing these documents over the years of your experience, have you become familiar with their usual form, the functional position that would usually be held by a person who would sign them or prepare them, and the specific organisations that created them in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I -- during my employment at ICTY, I visited several times the Bosnian Commission of Missing Persons in Sarajevo. I also visited cantonal courts in Tuzla and in Sarajevo. I visited Podrinje Identification Project. I visited ICMP several times. I spoke personally with individuals who were involved in the exhumation process itself and who were issuing the documents. I have worked myself with these documents directly in several cases in this Tribunal, so I think that -- at some point, I -- even my unit became a contact point for the OTP for exhumation materials.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to state with confidence that if a document had not been an authentic POD document, based on your expertise, that the Demographics Unit would not have relied upon it, in conducting this analysis?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. We -- it's for sure the case that if a non-authentic document would be provided, we would be able to see this fact and reject it. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see that we have about one minute till the break. This is a good stopping point in the examination. If you're so inclined, we could take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber is so inclined. Ms. Tabeau, we'll take a break, and we'll resume in 20 minutes from now. You're invited to follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break, and we resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Could the Court Officer now please call up P2796, MFI, at the bottom of page 2 in both languages?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While that is coming up, Dr. Tabeau, when did the Demographics Unit of the OTP close?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: In September 2011, with my departure from ICTY.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did this mean practically in terms of the demographics and proof of death data contained within the OTP?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the output of the unit's work stayed with the office and are available, can be used, but there is no continuation other than occasional visits of myself and others to finish pieces like Karadzic testimony or this testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the bottom of page 2 of your POD expert report which we see on our screens, it says that your colleague, Dr. Jan Zwierzchowski is mentioned. Is his work on this project the equivalent of the work of the previous active Demographics Unit team under your supervision?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Dr. Zwierzchowski was part of the demographic unit in the final stages of unit's existence. We have done together several reports and he was the one who -- for whom it was possible to come to the OTP and work on the POD report for the Mladic case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say, then, that the Demographics Unit was sort of resurrected for the purposes of preparing this -- this report, the reports for this case?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, Dr. Zwierzchowski spent approximately three and a half months working on the POD project. I myself spent more than one month working on this project, and on other issues. So it is certainly that we can say so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart, please, now, in Sanction to show us the bottom of slide 14.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the segment of your report prepared for the Stanisic and Simatovic case, which we have now as P2787, MFI, you set out a methodology underlying the creation of the integrated database. Was the POD project for the Mladic case carried out in a manner consistent with the methodology as set out in this segment of the Stanisic and Simatovic report?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. There were two parallel processes that were completed in the POD project. One process was the review of exhumation documents and missing persons records and linking them, based on the results of this review one by one manually, and there was a parallel process of using the integrated database and establishing links automatically between scheduled victims lists and the integrated database, in order to increase the quantity of information available for every scheduled victims. But the methodology was, in both cases, exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we can see in front of us the sources included in the integrated database. Can you explain in as simple as terms as possible what the integrated database is.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The integrated database is a match of a number of significant sources, large sources, reporting on victims of war. This database includes sources, such as the statistical death notifications, official death notifications reported by the families of the -- of the deceased. It includes all military lists. It includes missing persons records. It includes exhumation records and includes a number of sources compiled by other organisations, by NGOs, like MAG, Muslims Against Genocide, or Knjiga Nestalih Prijedor, which is the Prijedor Book of Missing. It also includes identification records for the Srebrenica victims, those based on DNA analysis. All these sources are large and extensive, and cover the war victims quite well, yet the -- even the merge of all these sources does not give a complete number of victims of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you to explain your role in the OTP with respect to the gathering of the data and the creation of the integrated database itself.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sources were collected by my unit and me personally over the years, and it was our idea to come up eventually with a good information system that could be used office-wide for tracing victims of war. The system that we eventually developed started with the population at the outbreak of the war, included a number of sources reported on victims as those in the integrated database, and ended with sources on post-war survivors. It was a tracking system that was meant to be used in all kinds of situations. Integrated database is just one step further in developing the -- the office-wide -- this information system. It just puts the sources together to make it easier to compile all kinds of lists of victims based on the merge and not on source by source and by source and by source.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have distributed to the Chamber and the Defence some handouts. These are not intended to be tendered at all. They're not uploaded. This is merely to assist in presenting the Chamber with the POD annex and how -- how this analysis was conducted. So I have one set in English and one set in B/C/S, which has been given to the Defence, and we're going to be referring to these handouts in conjunction with what we see on our screens. It will enable us to look at two documents at the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, we're going to turn to the POD annex to provide the Court with a few examples of how this analysis was done and to thereby explain how the annex can be used by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer please call up on our screens P2797, MFI. This is the POD annex. And please turn to e-court page 254 in English. The B/C/S version is on the handouts for the B/C/S speakers. Because the chart is so large, I would respectively show that we show the English on the screens. I'll note that it corresponds to pages 261 to 2 in B/C/S. Your Honours, this is reflected on handout 1 for your ease of reference. This page is part of the analysis for incident A7.2, in which the accused has been charged with the killing of a number of people in Hrustovo village, in Sanski Most, on or about 31 May 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, could I call your attention to victim 3 on this page, Almina Keranovic. As we move through the columns from the left, I would like to ask you some questions. Starting at the left we see the victim number, the last name, then first name, father's name, date and place of birth, and sex. Can you tell us what the source of information for this personal data would have been?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The source for these items is the population census, 1991, after having linked the personal information about this victim as reported on the scheduled list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, continuing over, we see the ICRC ID. Can you explain why neither Almina Keranovic nor her apparent relatives on this page have ICRC ID numbers?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the link with the ICRC list is obviously not established here through the census record, there is no ICRC number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea why that might be?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, sources are not complete. Some individuals reported the missing persons to the ICRC commission. Some others reported to BCMP commission and others perhaps to ICMP. So it is not necessarily that we will see every victim reported under the ICRC missing persons, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Continuing onto the next column, we see military status. On page 10 in English of your report and B/C/S page 13, you describe the military status as noted here in the POD annex. You say: "The military lists merely give a membership in the army but do not specify combat or non-combat circumstances of these deaths." Can you explain what you mean by this.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military lists were made for the purpose of registering deaths or missing of individuals, members of the army and others, like members of the Ministry of Defence or police, or even some people working for production sector providing services and goods to the army. The purpose of post-mortem pensions of these people. The place of death is reported very broadly as either being killed or missing. Circumstances of death are not discussed. Place of death is unavailable. So the military lists cannot be seen as a source that would contribute to the information on the fate of a missing person or a killed person. It is merely a source reporting on the membership.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question in this respect. The -- if someone does not appear on a military list, did you qualify that person as a civilian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is my understanding correct, that even when qualified as a civilian in this table, that is, not being registered in the military sources as a military, that they still have -- could have been combatants at the point of time when they went missing or died?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. It can go both directions. There might be a group of civilians who were in fact combatants, and of the militaries reported of the list, a group that were killed in non-combatant situations. And there is actually lots of information about it for Srebrenica projects that they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I might just ask a question. Madam Tabeau, you have explained to us that one -- the first five columns your -- for your -- the source for your first five columns was the population register. And then you said the ICRC ID number is missing for this person because this person was not necessarily reported to the ICRC. You indicated also that there were other places like ICMP and BCMP. I don't see any columns for those other sources on this chart. Now, am I right to say that the population register will only tell us that this person exists? Then that this person should be reported as missing to some kind of institution or authority, like the ICRC, which is mentioned here. And my question to you then is: How did we first determine that this person is missing? From which source? Because there's no -- the ICRC is not -- is not that source. Which source told us that this person is missing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. For this person, we have three documents or three sources that have been linked to -- to this person which are reported under POD source, 1, 2, 3, and source type is listed as first one autopsy report, court record of exhumation is the source number 2, and there is an entry from the integrated database as under the number 3. There is no source that would report this person as a missing person. Yet this person's body has been found in a grave which is explained here in the table in what grave and when and where. That simply means even though we don't have the missing person record for this person, and this information is unavailable, there is other evidence confirming what happened to this person. And it might be so that this person would have been reported to BCMP and ICMP which are not listed here. But somehow we were unable to link this information, to prove that the person was eventually reported as missing by somebody to an organisation. It is -- it -- this is all I can say. We -- we are not even able to tell whether or not this person was reported missing. It -- I can only say that the result of this exercise is showing that we didn't find a record of missing of this person in the sources used for this project.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do I then have to understand that the conclusion that we come to that this person is a missing person is -- is a victim of war is derived from the autopsy reports which tells us of the nature of his -- of her death?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not only that. If -- if we go through the -- the sources, yeah, there is an autopsy report that was made at the occasion of the exhumation of the body of this person which is describing the body exhumed in detail with the injuries and direct cause of death. There is court record of exhumation, which confirms what the autopsy report says, and there is a record from the integrated database under number 3. If -- if we look carefully at this source, in the last line under the -- the source type, integrated database, and there is an ID -- a record ID number there and there is in brackets number 4. Number 4. This tells us that we confirmed this person in source number 4 in the integrated database. In order to understand what kind of source was it, we need to go to Table 2 in the POD report, which is on page 11 in the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's handout page 2. It's the next page in your handout.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's exhumations 2009.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is the database or list or source called: "Exhumations 2009, merged." What does it mean? This means this is a summary list of actually missing persons who were confirmed by finding their remains in certain graves and identified in the exhumation process, and this summary list was provided to us by the BCMP commission, Bosnian Commission for Missing Persons, in addition to the actual exhumation reports and autopsy report that were collected completely independently from -- from this particular list. Yet these two came together. The summary information that was provided by the BCMP directly to my unit, and ended in the integrated database as a list of missing persons confirmed and identified in exhumations. This information came together consistently, fully with two other documents collected separately and studied directly in the POD project. So going back to Your Honour's question, even though there is no reference for this person, based on the ICRC record of missing, there is other evidence that tells us this person eventually was reported missing to somebody, in this case being BCMP commission, and the evidence is included in this material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Tabeau. My last question perhaps would be: How do we determine the date of death of this person as the 1st of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This determination is based on the records of the BCMP commission. The BCMP commission could have given us the data of missing, last seen of this person, but at the stage when the exhumation was completed, there was also, most likely, on-site investigation report available, which would include witness statements as to the incidents that led to burying -- killing people and burying them in an unmarked grave like this one. So the date of death here can be based actually also on this type of information, information about the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do I understand that the reference to source number 4 in the integrated database also tells us that the reliability of the time of death or disappearance is relatively low?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure that we can draw this conclusion from -- from -- from the fact that source 4 is reported. Where, for missing persons, the best we can have usually is the report on when they were last seen. Also, in -- in Srebrenica studies, the exact date of death is very hard to establish. All we have are the dates of disappearance as reported by informants, being, in case of ICRC, close relatives of the victims, or eye-witnesses. It's the same source for the BCMP commission. So the same source, not different. How reliable it is, it is only as reliable as -- as the memories of the family members are, but the exact date of death, yeah, I think there must be additional sources that can determine the exact date of death.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But in the sources in the integrated database, source number 4, exhumations 2009, merged, gives high reliability of the place of death or disappearance reporting and a low score for reliability of the time of death, disappearance reporting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The second page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the second page in the handout but not necessarily the second page in the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think Your Honour is talking about Table 2, right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, table 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. So it is indeed so that there is a certain hierarchy of sources that we used in the integrated database. ICRC list is mentioned under number 3, and exhumations 2009 under number 4. It is less reliable as information from statistical reporting, the two databases as we call them, death notifications because it's a different type of reporting. For known deaths we have death certificates signed by physicians who can determine very precisely when and how, what cause of death was. In case of missing persons, the best we can have is the ICRC and next after is -- after ICRC, BCMP commission comes as second. So I wouldn't call it completely unreliable because it is certainly not the same as the exact date of death, but it is just the best we can have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not saying it's not the best. I was talking about relatively unreliable --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- less reliable than other sources.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, less reliable, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I'm actually intending to take us step by step through the analysis for this victim. I hope that this will assist the Chamber even more extensively than Dr. Tabeau's answers. Perhaps I could take one step back and just clarify a few things for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The victim names on this annex are the names from the schedules in the indictment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And we will talk about additional victims a little bit later. I'll give Your Honours a example of an additional victim that that was found. This particular victim, Almina Keranovic, is from a schedule for A7.2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My other question, perhaps to clarify for -- for the Chamber, Dr. Tabeau, is it correct that the analysis as to the fate of Almina was done by a combined analysis of all three POD sources? That would be the autopsy report, the court record of exhumation and the integrated database analysed in conjunction?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let me -- I'm going take us through it. Before I take us to one of the underlying documents, could I just ask you one more question about military status. If the evidence that your team had analysed indicated that the person, the victim, indeed, died in a combat situation, you would have listed that person as excluded; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were sources like witness statements from court rulings that could indicate this and such victims would be then excluded from victims' lists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So we see the next two columns, as we've already started talking about, the POD source and the source type. I think -- I was going ask you to explain these columns, but I think you may have already done that in answer to the Chamber's questions. Looking at source 3, we see the number 4. And, for this, we've already gone to the handout page 2 to see which database in the integrated database this covers. Now, if we go to the next column, we see circumstances of death. Can you tell us where that information in the annex was taken from.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are -- this is information from the actual documents that were reviewed in the project, summarised next to each document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we're going to turn to those documents in just a moment. I just complete -- the columns. As we move to the right, we have the place of exhumation. Can you tell us where that comes from?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also from -- from the documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then we have a final conclusion.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is in this case confirmed, a confirmed victim of war. We developed a simple categorisation for victims. Confirmed is the most important category. For cases like this one, where all documents consistently indicate that the time of death, the place of death and circumstances of death as consistent with the incident, then the victim could be declared as confirmed. Other categories will be discussed in a minute. It is confirmed but mis-assigned, inconclusive, and exclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask one further question when we've gone through all the columns. The autopsy report, the -- the -- the various source, the three sources, are linked to this person. I do not find specifics on the identification of this person. Exhumation means that a body was exhumed. Autopsy report means that the cause of death was, to the extent possible, determined. But now where do we find the confirmation that the body which was exhumed and which -- which relates to the autopsy report is this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In the court record of exhumations, we will see in a minute, there is mention that a family -- family members and names of these members are given, identified the remains of this person as -- with name and other details. That is included in the court record, identification, and this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it, if it had been impossible to identify an exhumed body that it -- the person, which would then still be without a name, would not appear in this report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is very correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me be sure I understand the operation of the integrated database. As I understand it, looking at this page 1 and page 2 of the handout, the integrated database is the sum total of the sources of information about the missing person. And page 2 of the handout explains to us what is so integrated. That is FIS mortality database, RS mortality database, up to that. Is it therefore correct, on the first page here where we're dealing with this victim number 3, to mention integrated database as a source when, in fact, it's just a summary of the sources. The source is mentioned here as item number 4 on the integrated database, which is exhumations of 2009. Now, we seem to be using the integrated database as further proof of the source when, in fact, it is not. It is just a recording of the sources. Am I coming clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, absolutely. Absolutely. I think integrated database is -- in itself, is not a new source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Absolutely. That's my point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It reports on a number of sources that are integrated in it. And it gives the opportunity to review all the sources that reported on a given victim. At the same time, it can be used to pin-point the best source and take it as -- as -- for further analysis, information from that source. It is just a tool that we developed that makes it easier for analysts and for everybody to follow up on reporting of a given victim. And, as such - if I may finish - it gives a double-check to the review process of the actual exhumation documents. It can either corroborate or -- or -- yeah, disprove the results from -- from the individual documents. I am not sure I answered, but I tried.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thank you for that attempt. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I have one other question. Looking at the screen and focussing on number 6, Sejida Keranovic, we see as under the source type, integrated database and then between brackets (14). Do I have to understand that as being 1 and 4, where the sources are all single-digit numbers and therefore not to be read as 14 but as 1 and 4?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, perhaps to follow-up just with one question in relation to His Honour Judge Moloto's question, if Judge Moloto or any other member of the Chamber would like to see an underlying record that underlies these results that emerge from the integrated database, that would be technically possible. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the databases underlying the integrated database are collections of hundreds of thousands and, in some case, millions of individual records; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, integrated database itself comprises, as far as I remember, 100 -- about 190.000 individual records, representing different cases. This includes multiple records for -- for -- for a given victim as reported in various sources. So it is not millions in this particular database, but it is also linked with the population census and sources on survivors. It is part of a broader information system which, indeed, includes millions of records.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I ask the Court Officer to please call up source 1. We're going open each of the underlying documents to show to the Chamber how this was done. This is uploaded as 65 ter 12727A. We've created that as an excerpt of the full document. This document, Your Honours, can also be viewed on handout page 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Source 1 for Almina Keranovic is an autopsy report. Dr. Tabeau, is this autopsy report one of the many types of POD documents with which you have become familiar over the course of your work with the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar tells me that it's not in e-court. Perhaps it's not released. But it is just an excerpt --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- therefore, you are not tendering it as a separate exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: At the moment, we're not tendering it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then perhaps it would be good to have it uploaded and/or released in e-court as soon as possible so that we have an opportunity to later look at it, if need be.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have been informed by Ms. Stewart that it has been released now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We have it on our handout. When the Court Officer is ready, I would ask the Court Officer to turn in the English to page 2 on our screens, but we see the entire document on handout page 3. As we look down at the bottom of this autopsy report we can see two conclusions at the bottom. The death was violent and a direct consequence of the shattering of the head. The head was shattered by a shot from a fire-arm from contact range.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this where the information entered into the POD annex in the column entitled "Circumstances of death" according to the source originated?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the source for this information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And now I would ask Your Honours to turn to the next page in the handout. If the Court Officer is able to, I would ask her to call up 65 ter 12728, pages 6 and 7 in B/C/S, and page 6 in English. This is the court record of exhumation, the second source for Almina. I will note for the record that we have tendered this court record of exhumation in the 31 October 2013 residual bar table motion and also that one excerpt from this document has already been admitted as P2496. As we look at handout 4, we turn to the court record of exhumation for Hrustovo 1. This court record of exhumation is a document which covers a number of victims, the bodies exhumed from that mass grave. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in relation to His Honour Judge Moloto's question - I believe, unless it was His Honour Judge Orie, I think it was Judge Moloto - we see above body number 7 an infant with no name and therefore we would not in that case, for example, be able to link that only on this document if that were a victim on our list; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would be correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now below we see body number 8, that of Almina Keranovic. Is this now where the information entered in the POD annex in the column on circumstances of death from the court record of exhumation originated?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As we see, there is a mention here of the identification by -- of this victim by family members Ramiza Keranovic and Ala Meradanovic. And the full victim name with the date of birth, place of residence, names of father and mother are included.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could I ask you, what in this material would have led to you confirm her as a victim, because your confirmation, as you explained in your reports, is not only that Almina Keranovic is dead but also that her death occurred in the circumstances of this Scheduled Incident, A7.2. Could you tell us what in this material led to you confirm her as a victim of A7.2.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a description of injuries and cause of death in this document, and it says death was violent and immediate as a result of the head having been shattered. The head was shattered by a shot from a fire-arm at contact range. So this leaves no doubt as to the way that victim died. It is just that we took it and moved and placed in the annex that was prepared in the POD project, and then it's easy to see immediately what the cause of death was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in addition to the cause of death, the link to the date and time, place of death, came from which source, in relation to Almina?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we discussed earlier today, this come -- come -- came from the BCMP records of the missing persons, and this is how the person was reported by the family members and other -- likely other witnesses to this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I also -- can we agree also that the approximate date or the date of death of this person is 1985 as mentioned here on the -- on the court record? And not 1975 as mentioned on the autopsy report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is most certainly a typo which is incorrect because there is also reference in the reports to the age of the victim, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In both there is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In both, yes. So it is 1985, not 1975.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I further ask you whether you have considered any possible inconsistencies between the various sources. Just to give you an example -- well, just to look at this one, I see that the autopsy report describes the clothing as a black jacket; whereas the court report describes as the clothing wearing a red button-up jacket, a different colour. Would have you considered that, or would you have ignored that? Not to say that for that reason they are different persons and not to say that it may be rather difficult after a certain period of time to determine the colour, but did you notice it, and did you consider it in any way in your findings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we studied the whole document, so every part was taken into account, and this type of inconsistencies are quite common. As Your Honour mentioned, it is related to the long time since -- since the death that have passed. It is very difficult to identify and describe the clothes as they were initially. I think there is a core information here that is consistent across all the sources. This is the information about what kind of person this victim is. The age is clearly determined. The cause of death is clearly established. There is consistency in the reporting by the family members about the time of death and the place of death. There is a report on the missing. All together, it adds up to a very consistent picture. So we -- in this situation, the conclusion is the description of clothing is less significant because it is less reliable. But inconsistencies, as Your Honour mentioned, across the sources are there. Absolutely. Are there. And therefore we developed this categorisation and highlighted cases that cannot be considered consistent, the confirmed cases. There are exclusions and inconsistent cases that we also flagged in the annex. These are cases which didn't coming together that well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you made an assessment as to whether inconsistencies that were found are of such significance that you would have to put a question mark to the bodies described to be the same bodies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, to add to this discussion, would it -- each -- it seems from your report that each incident was analysed as a whole. How would the total analysis of all of the victims of a particular incident assist you in analysing the -- the fate of any one of the individual victims of that incident? Would that also assist or was that not -- not important?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. The general description of every incident did matter, even though the description as available from the indictment is not very extensive, but important elements are there. The place of the incident, the date of incident, the type of what happened. So we also search for consistency of this kind of broader picture in the report on the missing of -- of these individuals and in the exhumation records, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I now ask the Court Officer, please, to call up the POD annex again. That is P2797, MFI, and please show us page 91 in English. This will correspond to pages 108 and 9 in B/C/S, and it is on handout 5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, we are looking at this page in front of us which refers to Scheduled Incident A4.4, in which the accused has been charged with the killing of a number of men in or around the school in Grabovica on or about the 3rd of November, 1992. If we look at the list of victims in the POD annex, we see that, as per the indictment schedules, there are only five named scheduled victims, but the POD project has -- has revealed 142 additional victims for this incident under A4.4. So before we go into one example, could I just ask you to advise the Chamber generally how it was determined that these individuals were additional victims of this incident.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The search for additional victims was conducted in exactly the same way as the search for a -- for regular victims included in the schedules. So the initial point was a full-system search in the OTP resources for relevant documents that would be reporting on -- on the circumstances of death of people of certain incidents. This full search was also -- was also bringing additional results when we were looking for regular victims, scheduled victims at this occasion, certain documents were identified in which more victims were reported. So this was one approach. Certainly we also had other possibilities. Having the integrated database made it possible for us to search for victims according to date and place as defined in the incidents lists, like ICRC list are very easy from this point of view to search through and to come up with broader lists of victims reported disappeared at the same dates, the same places. Further, when studying documents like exhumation reports and whole sets of autopsy reports, next to the regular scheduled victims, there were additional victims documented in exactly same way. So there have been very good reasons for us to decide that, in addition to the scheduled victims, there must have been other victims, not included in the schedules. That was the procedure that we used when searching for additional victims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, calling our attention to victim 139 on the page in front of us, that is Sulejman Turudic, we see under the integrated database entry four different databases. And you explain in your report and you've just explained to the Chamber that this means the victim is reported in four separate databases.
